summaryText:
In week four of the series My Wounds Won't Win, Pastor Travis Hearn taught a message titled Never Waste a Wound. The service opened with a warm welcome from Erica, who encouraged the online campus family to keep walking through the series, invite others, and stay committed to what God is doing. Pastor Travis began in prayer, asking God to speak through his words and to bring healing and wholeness.

Anchoring the message in 2 Corinthians 1:3-4, Pastor Travis explained that God comforts us in our troubles so that we can comfort others, and he described this as ministry. He pointed to the risen Jesus, who kept the scars in his hands and side even in a glorified body, and who invited Thomas to see them in John 20:27. Those scars became a testimony. God does not always erase every scar, but he can transform what it means.

Pastor Travis shared three main thoughts. First, a wound is not sent by God, but it can be used by God. He noted that hardship comes in a fallen world and used valleys, fires, and storms from Scripture as pictures of trials. Drawing on John 10:10, he contrasted the enemy's aim to steal, kill, and destroy with Jesus' promise of abundant life. Romans 8:28, the story of Job, and Joseph's words in Genesis 50:20 illustrated redemption. God does not pretend pain never happened, but he rewrites the story and brings purpose from it.

Second, God wants to use our hurts to help others. Pastor Travis said healing is meant to become a river, not a reservoir. He encouraged people to share testimonies of freedom with those still struggling. He invited those who had been set free from various struggles to stand, showing the power of the church family, and he highlighted the value of midweek gatherings where people minister to one another.

Third, we should not build a monument to our pain, but a ministry from it. God never intended pain to become our personality, but a platform. Pastor Travis pointed to Moses, Rahab, Peter, and Paul as examples of God using unlikely people. He asked whether our wounds might be entrusted to us as a form of stewardship, so that someone else's freedom, hope, or healing could be found through our story.

The message closed with prayer, as listeners were invited to surrender their wounds to God with open hands, trusting him with their pain and their future. Pastor Travis also offered an invitation to begin a relationship with Jesus. Erica ended by encouraging everyone to carry the message into the week, invite someone to the final week of the series, and take next steps through the connection options shown on screen.
mainPoints: Your wound was not sent by God, but it can be used by God, because he is a Redeemer who brings purpose out of pain.
God comforts us so that we can comfort others: our hurts and healing become ministry that helps set other people free.
Do not build a monument to your pain. Build a ministry from it, so that your wound becomes a platform and a testimony of God's faithfulness.

versesMentioned.text: Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, this is your true and proper worship.

Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.
After he said this, he was taken up before their very eyes, and a cloud hid him from their sight.
Then he said to Thomas, "Put your finger here; see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side. Stop doubting and believe."
Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar leaped to his feet in amazement and asked his advisers, "Weren't there three men that we tied up and threw into the fire?" They replied, "Certainly, Your Majesty." He said, "Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods."
He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, "Quiet! Be still!" Then the wind died down and it was completely calm.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.
And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.
I know that my redeemer lives, and that in the end he will stand on the earth.
You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.
Moses said to the LORD, "Pardon your servant, Lord. I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since you have spoken to your servant. I am slow of speech and tongue."
By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies, was not killed with those who were disobedient.
Those who accepted his message were baptized, and about three thousand were added to their number that day.
His master replied, "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!"
Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, because God has said, "Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you."
Then he said to them all: "Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me."

Monday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 1:4 (NIV): "...who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God."
Monday.focus: God comforts us so that we can comfort others.
Monday.action: Write down one way God has comforted you in a hard season. Then think of one person who might be going through something similar.
Monday.prayer: Father of compassion, thank you for the comfort you have given me. Show me who needs that comfort today, and help me to share it with kindness. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Romans 8:28 (NIV): "And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose."
Tuesday.focus: God is a Redeemer who brings purpose out of pain.
Tuesday.action: Quietly name one hurt or disappointment you have been carrying. Open your hands in prayer and surrender it to God, trusting him with it.
Tuesday.prayer: Lord, I give you this wound with open hands. I trust you to bring good and purpose from it. Help me not to let my pain have the final word. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: John 20:27 (NIV): "Put your finger here; see my hands... Stop doubting and believe."
Wednesday.focus: Scars can become a testimony of God's faithfulness.
Wednesday.action: Think of a time God brought you through a difficult season. Write a few sentences about what he did, so you are ready to share it when the opportunity comes.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, thank you that your scars are a sign of victory. Help me to see my own healing as evidence of your faithfulness. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Genesis 50:20 (NIV): "You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives."
Thursday.focus: Shift from asking why this happened to asking who I can help.
Thursday.action: Send an encouraging text or make a short call to someone who may be struggling. Simply let them know you are thinking of them and praying for them.
Thursday.prayer: God, turn my question from why to who. Use what I have walked through to bring encouragement and hope to someone else. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Psalm 23:4 (NIV): "Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me."
Friday.focus: God is present with us in every valley, fire, and storm.
Friday.action: Pray with or for one person today, whether a family member, friend, or coworker. Invite them to a midweek gathering or to watch a service with you.
Friday.prayer: Lord, thank you that you are with me in every valley. Help me to walk alongside others so that none of us feels alone. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Matthew 25:21 (NIV): "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things."
Saturday.focus: Stewarding my story for God's glory.
Saturday.action: Take a few minutes to review the week. Ask God how he might want to use your story, and invite someone to join you for the final week of the series next Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: Father, help me to steward my story well. I refuse to waste what you have redeemed. Use my life to point others to you. Amen.

title: How God Can Turn Your Pain Into Purpose | Never Waste a Wound
